title: test(ui): pin the Bore ring plan in the detect-holes note tests
body:
## What changed

The post-merge gate on `8719d8b7a` failed in two UI tests of `crates/ui/src/detect_holes_note_tests.rs`.

Cause: PR #1839 (#1566, merge `56ee418b`) changed the Bore law on purpose. In `crates/motion/src/machining2d/bore_core.rs`, `bore_leaves_core` now reads `bore_ring_count(...).is_none()`. Bore clears a wide hole with concentric rings. A hole is refused only past 4096 rings, or when the tool has no floor band. In `crates/app/src/operation/bore_reach.rs`, `keep_borable` uses the same plan. A 4 mm end mill now keeps the Ø74.3 hole. The two UI tests still expected the old one-ring limit (Ø12).

Which side was wrong: the tests. The product refuses each hole that the ring plan cannot clear, so no refusal was lost.

The tests now pin the new law:
- The fixture tool is a Ø10 bull-nose with a 4.999 mm corner (`BB-1000-R1` with its corner changed).
- A Ø74.3 through hole is stored. The corner reaches R3.001 at the floor plane, so the plan uses 14 rings.
- A Ø24 blind hole is skipped by name. Its floor band is R0.001, so it needs 8750 rings. The limit is Ø16.554.
- A plate with only the blind hole is refused, and nothing is stored.

The fixture builder now takes a blind floor height for each cell. The `#[test]` count stays at two.

Decision entry: `docs/decisions/1909-bore-wide-hole-tests.md`.

## Readings

- Both tests pass locally. Each test takes about 0.02 s.
- The 78 s in the post-merge log is not the cost of the tests. Locally, the old failing tests also ended in 0.01 s. No heavy-lane move is necessary.

## Pinning tests

- `detect_holes_note_tests::detect_holes_on_a_bore_op_stores_the_wide_through_hole_and_names_the_one_past_the_ring_budget`
- `detect_holes_note_tests::detect_holes_on_a_bore_op_with_only_a_hole_past_the_ring_budget_is_refused`

Gate: `cargo xtask gate test detect_holes_on_a_bore_op --crate camcraft-ui` is green on the final head. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- The full ui suites and the batch tier. The next post-merge run checks them.
- The zero-floor-band refusal (a ball nose at a blind floor). The Bore tool door refuses a ball nose at create, so the UI cannot reach it. The app unit test `detect_refuses_a_blind_ball_floor_but_keeps_the_through_hole` pins it.

## Follow-up

- #1910: the `detect_holes` row of the camcraft-mcp skill still states the one-ring limit. That file is a process file, so it is not in this PR.

title: test(post): pin the G76 readings that two published manuals settle
body:
## What changed

- New test file `crates/app/tests/lathe_post_g76_sources.rs`. It pins three G76 readings that two published manuals of two different makers settle.
- The G76 fixture and the control model move from `lathe_post_g76_schedule.rs` to `crates/app/tests/common/g76.rs`. The schedule suite was at the 400-line limit. Its tests do not change.
- Decision file `docs/decisions/1842-g76-schedule-sources.md` gives the sources and the readings.
- The post, the goldens and the posted G-code do not change. This PR does not touch `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`. Thus no conflict with #1866 or #468 is expected.

## Sources

- S1: FANUC Series 0i-MODEL F Operator's Manual, Lathe System, B-64604EN-1/01, section 4.2.7 "Multiple Threading Cycle (G76)", Fig. 4.2.7 (a) and (b).
- S2: Siemens SINUMERIK ISO Turning Programming Manual 07/2022, A5E52211627B AA, "Multiple-thread cutting cycle (G76)", Fig. 4-25 and 4-26, pages 87-89.
- Contrast only: Hurco WinMax Lathe G76, Haas lathe G76, GSK988TA G76, LinuxCNC G76.

## Readings

1. Start point and Z shift: settled. The post agrees. The cycle starts at A above the crest point B. Each deeper pass starts `depth * tan(a/2)` further along the travel (one edge cuts).
2. End point: settled. The post agrees. Every pass ends at the programmed end point D. The kernel lays shallower passes short of D. The control cuts them to D, inside the groove of the root pass. This removes no extra material. #1896 tracks the simulation detail.
3. Minimum depth: settled. The post agrees. Q(dmin) clamps the cut of one pass below the pass before it.
4. Internal rounding of `dd * sqrt(n)`: open. No source states it. The post's guard stays.

## Pinning tests

- `lathe_post_g76_sources::each_pass_starts_on_the_crest_flank_line_along_the_travel`
- `lathe_post_g76_sources::every_pass_runs_to_the_posted_end_z_inside_the_root_pass`
- `lathe_post_g76_sources::the_minimum_depth_clamps_the_cut_of_one_pass` (it also proves that the other clamp reading gives a different ladder)

## Gate

- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test lathe_post_g76_schedule --test lathe_post_g76_sources`: 7 + 3 passed. The golden `thread_g76_area.nc` did not change.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test lathe_post_g76_schedule --test lathe_post_g76_sources -- -D warnings`: clean.

- Reading 4 stays open on #1842.
- Clippy ran on the two touched test binaries only, not on `--all-targets`. The other app test binaries also compile `common/g76.rs`.

title: fix(post): write each Fanuc-family length word with a decimal point
body:
## What changed

The five Fanuc-family posts now write each length word with a decimal point: `Z14.`, never `Z14`. Fanuc parameter 3401 bit 0 (DPI) sets how the control reads a word with no point. With DPI=0 the control reads `Z14` as 0.014 mm, and a rapid to it goes almost to Z0. With the point, DPI=0 and DPI=1 read the same value.

- `assets/posts/fanuc.cps`, `haas.cps`, `mazak.cps`, `doosan-dnm.cps`: a new helper `pt` adds the point. The length format `fu` and the angle format `fa` use it. The helper `fn` keeps the old trimmed text for comments and for macro-B expressions (a macro-B constant is not scaled by DPI).
- `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`: the same for X (diameter), Z, I, K, R, the C angle, the feed per revolution and the thread lead (`F2.`), and the G76 R finish allowance. The G76 P/Q and G83 Q words stay in whole least increments: the control documents these addresses as "no decimal point".
- Feeds per minute are not changed (`F300`, or in/min at two decimals).
- `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`: a new law bullet "A length word carries its decimal point (#1836)".
- `docs/decisions/1836-fanuc-decimal-point.md`: the decision entry.

## The golden changes

All golden diffs of the Fanuc-family posts add only a trailing `.` to whole-number length, angle, lead and feed-per-rev words (for example `G00 X10 Y0 Z5` becomes `G00 X10. Y0. Z5.`). No value changes. No block is added or removed. The probe macro lines (`IF[ABS[#5063-25]GT0.001]...`, `#190=#100+17`) do not change. The goldens of the other posts do not change.

`crates/post/tests/explain_fanuc_family.rs` now writes its Explain golden when `WRITE_GOLDEN` is set, as the other golden tests do.

## Pinning tests

`crates/post/tests/decimal_point_fanuc_family.rs`:
- `the_mill_posts_write_a_whole_number_length_with_its_point` (fanuc, haas, mazak, doosan-dnm: `Z14.`, `Z-8.`, `X30.`, and no motion word with a bare length)
- `the_mill_posts_write_a_whole_number_inch_length_with_its_point` (the same four posts in inch: `Z1.`, `Z-1.`)
- `the_lathe_post_writes_a_whole_number_length_and_feed_per_rev_with_its_point` (fanuc-lathe: `X30. Z14.`, `Z-8.`, `F1.`)

title: fix(post): refuse a bore dwell where G86 has no dwell word; pin G86 per post (#1445)
body:
## What changed

This is slice 2 of #1445: the boring cycle (G86: feed in, spindle stop, rapid out). The `Bore` cycle kind was already on main. This slice pins it per post and closes two dwell gaps.

- `assets/posts/{fanuc,haas,mazak,doosan-dnm,sinumerik}.cps`: a bore with a dwell is refused by name. Before this change, these posts wrote `P<ms>` on G86. The published Fanuc and Haas G86 formats have no P word, so the control dropped the dwell without a message. A bore with no dwell posts as before.
- tormach and grblhal keep `G86 ... P<seconds>` (the LinuxCNC G86 takes P as a dwell in seconds).
- The expanding posts (heidenhain, tinyg, carvera) do not change.
- New door `OpParams::dwell_refusal` (`crates/app/src/operation/types/dwell.rs`): a drilling dwell is a time from 0 to 3600 s (`MAX_DWELL_S`). `CreateOperation` and `EditOperationParams` refuse other values by name. MCP `edit_operation` uses the same command, so it refuses them too. The project loader does not use this door, so an old project still opens.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1445-boring-g86.md`.

The default posted output does not change. No existing NC or CL golden changed.

## Sources

- NIST IR 6556 (The NIST RS274NGC Interpreter v3), G86.
- The LinuxCNC G-code reference (G86 with P in seconds).
- The public Fanuc 30i operator manual (B-63944EN) and the Haas mill programming workbook, for the G86 address words.

No vendor post file or CAM output was read.

## How tested

- `crates/post/tests/bore_cycle.rs` (7 tests): the stream round trip, G86 and no other cycle on the canned posts, the by-name dwell refusal on the Fanuc family and Sinumerik, `P0.5` on tormach and grblhal, the expanded chain with its dwell, the refusal on posts without drilling, and new goldens in `crates/post/tests/golden/bore/` (fanuc, haas, heidenhain, sinumerik, grblhal, tormach).

title: feat(2d): rest machining on the 2D Pocket operation
body:
Fork synced at v0.20.0 (process files at PROCESS_VERSION 71).

## What changed

The 2D Pocket can now cut only what a larger previous tool left. It uses the rest generator of #1446 (`machining2d::rest_pocket`).

- **Parameter.** `OpParams::Pocket` has a new optional `rest` group: previous tool diameter, its corner radius, the stock it left on the walls, and the rest allowance. `None` is off. Off is the default and the plain pocket.
- **Undoable edit.** You change the group through `EditOperationParams`. Undo and redo restore it.
- **Project file.** The key is `rest` (an object). A file without the key reads as off, so the file version does not change.
- **Stamp.** The stamp writes the group (byte `0xD7`) only when it is on. Each value of the group changes the stamp.
- **Generation.** When the group is on, generation calls `rest_pocket`. Its note ("rest machining trusts the entered previous tool ...") goes into the path notes.
- **Refusals by name, in the generator's own words, when you make, edit or retool the operation** (not only at Generate):
  - a previous tool that is not larger than the operation's tool (new `rest_gate`, run from `tool_gate` and from the edit);
  - a value that is negative or not finite, a previous tool diameter that is 0 or less, or a corner radius larger than the previous tool's radius;
  - the Zigzag or Adaptive strategy;
  - pre-drilled entry with rest machining on (`REST_PREDRILLED`). `rest_pocket` does not read the holes, and the program must not drop a user setting without saying so.
- **Motion crate.** `RestParams` has a new `validate_alone` (the checks that do not need a tool, plus "the previous tool diameter must be positive"). The strategy check moved into a public `rest_strategy`. Its text did not change.
- **MCP.** `edit_operation` sets the group (`"rest": null` turns it off). There is a new row in the camcraft-mcp skill. Area: mcp.
- **Not in this PR: the dialog group.** It is not part of "Done means", and it needs before/after screenshots and the UI gate. The page keeps the group as it is when you apply the page. Follow-up: #1815.

## How tested

The new pinning tests are in `crates/app/tests/rest_pocket.rs`:
- `the_rest_pass_cuts_only_the_corners_posts_and_matches_its_golden`: the fixture is a 60 x 40 pocket with 3 mm corners. A 12 mm end mill roughs it, then a 4 mm end mill does the rest pass. The golden is `pocket_rest_corners.cl`. All cuts stay in the corners. The program posts and the verification report is clean.
- `read_against_the_simulated_roughing_pass`: the roughing pass is simulated first on the stock dexel grid. Then:
  - no rapid of the rest pass hits stock;
  - every plunge goes down on floor that is already clear, and its rim touches stock for no more than one level;
  - all 8 rings (4 corners x 2 levels) cut stock, and air is less than half of each ring.
- `the_group_is_an_undoable_edit_and_the_project_file_keeps_it`
- `a_previous_tool_that_is_not_larger_is_refused_by_name_at_the_edit_and_the_retool` (edit, create and retool)
- `values_and_strategies_the_rest_pass_cannot_run_are_refused_by_name`
- `mcp_sets_refuses_undoes_and_saves_the_group` (set, refuse, save, reopen, null, undo)

Other tests:
- `operation::rest_op_tests::the_rest_group_moves_the_stamp`
- `crates/motion/tests/rest2d.rs`: a new case for a 0 mm previous tool.

Mutation check: I deleted each new refusal line, the stamp line and the generation line one at a time, ran the test that pins it, and saw it fail. Then I restored the file and compared it with a backup. All 11 failed when deleted and were restored byte for byte: the motion "must be positive" check, rest_op's three refusals, sane's `named_refusal` and `is_sane` lines, `rest_gate` in `tool_gate`, `rest_gate` in the edit, the refusal arm inside `rest_gate`, the `0xD7` stamp block, and the `rest_pocket` call in generation.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick` plans almost the whole workspace for this diff, so I ran the touched suites by name instead (motion: lib, rest2d, machining2d, predrilled_entry, corner_arc_radius, optimal_load, solid_law; app: lib, rest_pocket, golden_cl, arc_turn_params, predrilled_entry, project_roundtrip, roughing2d, adaptive_trochoid, mcp, mcp_pockets, pocket_recognition, operations, commands_undo, tool_gate, tool_law, verify, solid_law_goldens, heights, tilt, corner_blend, climb_direction, area_controls, pick_agnostic, pocket_overhead, units_in_refusals, lead_approach, level_links, whole_model_pocket, recorded_post_streams; ui: lib, edge_loop_pick, operations). All green. Clippy `-D warnings` on camcraft-motion, camcraft-app and camcraft-ui (all targets): clean.

The existing pocket goldens do not change (`golden_cl`, `adaptive_trochoid`, `roughing2d` and the others in the list above).

## What I did not test

- I did not run the program on a machine, and I did not take screenshots (there is no UI change).
- Two things I measured but did not fix, because they are generator behaviour and not part of this slice:
  - The inner leg of each corner ring crosses floor that the 12 mm tool already cleared: 6.7 mm of a 14.8-15.3 mm ring. Follow-up: #1816.
  - On each level, 2 of the 4 corner plunges touch rest material at the rim. The tool axis is over cleared floor. Entry from cleared space belongs to #1490.

title: feat(sim): sinker body electrode - outline atom, tool record and electrode from faces
body:
fork synced at v0.20.0 · process files at PROCESS_VERSION 71 · branch from `upstream/main` 03dc12c6

## What changed

A sinker electrode can now be a BODY: a closed outline extruded along Z. Before this PR the stock sim burned a rectangular face only (the box atom of #541), and `electrode_from_faces` refused each cavity that was not an axis-aligned rectangle (`NON_RECTANGULAR`, which named this issue).

1. **Sim atom** (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/dexel_outline.rs`, `stock_sim::simulate_outline`). The outline, grown by the spark gap, is swept along straight chords through the column grid. The result is exact at each column centre: nothing is sampled. The grown section is the inside of the polygon joined with a stadium on each edge. A chord meets a stadium in one interval, in closed form. The face height is linear along the chord, so the lowest height is at the first or the last covered parameter. An arc, a posed move, a non-finite move, a bad gap and an outline that is no section are refused by name before a column is lowered. The box atom is not changed.
2. **Tool record** (`Tool::outline`, `crates/tools/src/electrode_outline.rs`). Points in mm about the burn point; empty for a rectangular face. `diameter` and `width` stay the X and Y extents of the outline, and the outline is centred on the burn point. The record's door (`is_sane`, `torch_refusal`) refuses by name an outline that is no simple section (3 to 1024 points) and sizes that do not agree with it. The key `outline` goes through the project file, the library file, the tools crate's catalog reader and the MCP `add_tool` / `edit_tool` definitions (additive, written only when stated). The operation stamp digests the points.
3. **`electrode_from_faces`** (`crates/motion/src/sinker_electrode_body.rs`). A cavity that is no axis-aligned rectangle yields a body electrode. The obstruction check uses the cavity's own outline as the column. The size law of #543 judges an outline on its extents (`Undersize::outline`).
4. **The program verdict** burns a record that has an outline with the outline atom, and a record without one with the box atom. The field eye still refuses a program with an electrode (#548).

The decisions are in `docs/decisions/1152-electrode-body.md`.

## Done means

- A rounded-corner pocket's faces yield an electrode whose burn `simulate_document` judges clean: `a_rounded_pockets_faces_yield_an_electrode_whose_burn_is_judged_clean`.
- A burn of the same electrode in a smaller cavity is convicted as a gouge: `the_same_electrode_in_a_smaller_cavity_is_convicted_as_a_gouge`.
- The non-rectangular refusal of #547 is gone: `a_cavity_that_is_no_rectangle_yields_a_body_electrode` (a rotated rectangle, an L, a chamfered corner).

## How tested

Pinning tests:

- `crates/sim/tests/stock_outline.rs` (new, 5 tests): a plunge burns the section grown by the gap and nothing else; a rectangular outline burns what the box atom burns; a sampled oracle with an independent distance rule and inside rule bounds a sloping sweep from both sides; each refusal is by name and leaves the grid untouched; garbage input burns or refuses and never raises a column.
- `crates/tools/src/electrode_outline.rs` (2 unit tests), `crates/tools/src/catalog_asset_tests.rs::a_catalog_electrode_keeps_its_outline`.
- `crates/motion/src/sinker_electrode_body_tests.rs` (new, 4 tests), `sinker_electrode_tests.rs` (`a_cavity_that_is_no_rectangle_yields_a_body_electrode`, `a_body_electrodes_column_is_the_cavitys_outline_not_its_bounds`), `sinker_undersize.rs::sinker_undersize_judges_an_outline_on_its_extents`. The existing electrode fuzz test now also derives body electrodes.
- `crates/app/tests/sinker_electrode_body.rs` (new, 5 tests): the two "Done means" tests; an L cavity; a diamond cavity; the project file round trip and the stale burn after a re-cut outline. Each clean verdict has a contrast: the rectangle of the same two sizes is convicted in the pocket's corners (rounded pocket) and in the notch (L).
- `crates/app/tests/sinker_electrode_mcp.rs::a_rounded_pocket_yields_a_body_electrode_over_mcp`, `crates/app/tests/tool_library.rs::a_body_electrodes_outline_roundtrips_through_the_library`, `crates/app/src/stock_sim_held_tests.rs::the_outline_atom_burns_a_column_grid_and_a_field_refuses_it_by_name`.

Mutation check: 51 mutations, one for each new refusal line, stamp line and dispatch line. Each mutation was applied, the pinning suite was run and was red, the file was restored and compared byte for byte with its backup. 51 of 51 red.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, 5 steps. The first run: tools, sim, motion and app suites green (21 min), the ui step red with a compile error (the tool page's draft built a `Tool` without the new field). The fix makes the draft carry the outline (`ToolUi::outline`), pinned by `crates/ui/tests/sinker_setup.rs::the_tool_draft_carries_a_body_electrodes_outline_through_an_apply`. The ui step was then run again with `--only ui` (10 suites): green. Only `crates/ui` changed between the two runs. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`: clean. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## What was not exercised

- A real EDM control. The conditions are synthetic and the blocks are built in code.
- An orbit or a side burn of a body electrode through an operation. The lateral sweep of the atom is pinned in the sim crate against the oracle.
- The UI pages. No page generates, shows or edits an outline (#548 owns the sinker pages). The tool page's draft carries the outline through an Apply (pinned); an edit of the X or Y size of a body electrode on the page is refused by name by the record's door.
- The batch gate, the release lanes and the pixel snapshots.
- Windows and macOS.

## Limits, each refused by name or filed

- A wall picked as its welded (curved) face: refused as before. #1808.
- A drafted wall or a stepped floor: refused as before. #1809.
- A finish pass of a cavity with sharp corners that are not square to the axes: the size law refuses it as under size. #1810.
- An outline of more than 1024 points: refused by name.
- An older build reads a body electrode as the rectangle of its two sizes (it skips the unknown key). That rectangle contains the outline, so the old build burns more, not less.

No new command, so no new MCP tool. `electrode_from_faces` answers `electrode.shape` and `electrode.outline`. The camcraft-mcp skill's table is a process file and is not touched here.

Changelog: A sinker electrode can be a body: `electrode_from_faces` makes an outline electrode for a cavity that is not an axis-aligned rectangle (a rounded-corner pocket, an L, a rotated rectangle), the tool record carries the outline through the project file, the library and MCP, and the program verdict burns it with a new outline atom.

Effort: max (not escalated)

Fixes #1152

## Tool draft before / after

Authentic captures of the egui tool editor using the same synthetic L-section electrode (10 × 8 mm). Both captures edit X to 12 mm and click the editor's Apply. The rectangular preview is unchanged: it does not visualize the electrode's XY outline.

Before: reproduction of the former draft-transfer behavior, clearing the draft outline before Apply. The edit succeeds (E-L becomes Ø12); the stored tool loses its section and becomes a rectangular electrode.

![Before: former draft behavior reproduced](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/18b32fc1/1811/before.png)

After: the current draft retains the outline. Apply refuses the inconsistent X extent by name, and the stored E-L remains Ø10 with its original section. The red refusal is visible below Apply.

![After: outline preserved and inconsistent extent refused](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/18b32fc1/1811/after.png)

Images are stored only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch. Captured with a temporary test harness running the shipping shell and real Apply button. The harness asserted both stored outcomes and was removed after capture. The permanent behavior pin is `the_tool_draft_carries_a_body_electrodes_outline_through_an_apply`.

title: feat(sim): carry machined stock into a setup turned side-on
body:
## What changed

A setup that stands the part on its edge can now take "What Setup1 leaves behind" as its stock. The turn is a quarter turn about X or Y from the setup before it. Before this change the carry was refused by name (`CARRY_TURN_REFUSAL`).

**camcraft-sim** (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/carry_side.rs`, new):

- `SideTurn` is one of the sixteen side-on quarter turns. `CarryTurn` is a lattice turn or a side turn.
- `Body::carry_side` reads the column body again along the new tool axis:
  - The level axis that stays level is re-indexed, centre onto centre.
  - The old heights become slabs of one cell, centred on the old Z range. A face inside a slab counts the slab whole.
  - The old level axis becomes the height. The top and the floor are the hull of the old column centres that hold material. Each end moves out to the next centre that holds no material, or to the lattice edge. A cavity between the ends is filled.
- The carried body is never smaller than the body the columns hold. It is at most one grid cell larger on a turned face. The raw faces of a box stock at the lattice edge are read exactly.
- The field engine refuses a side-on turn by name (`FIELD_SIDE_CARRY_REFUSAL`). The shipped engine is the column engine.
- `CARRY_TURN_REFUSAL` has shorter words: "the stock simulation carries machined stock only through quarter turns (steps of 90° about X, Y or Z)". A turn off the quarter is still refused and the app still names the turn and the two setups.

**camcraft-app**:

- `stock_sim_carry.rs`: `carry_turn` returns a `CarryTurn`. The program walk judges the body before a side-on turn and keeps those gouges for the final verdict. The hull can hide a gouge that an earlier setup cut. This is the same fold that a block left for a new block gets (#320).
- `side_on_note` adds a note line to the gate: the stock was turned side-on, and what the verdict reads.
- `rest/across.rs` and `rest.rs` hold a `CarryTurn`. The rest reading, the judged stock, the prior plan and the carried block follow the same turn. The `Debug` text of a lattice turn is unchanged, so no shipped stamp moves.

No user-facing command is new. No MCP tool is owed.

## How it was tested

Pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/setup_carry_side.rs`
  - `a_faced_plate_carries_side_on_with_its_volume_and_verdict` (the "Done means" test: volume, size, clean verdict, and a 1 mm gouge in Setup2 is found)
  - `a_gouge_cut_before_a_side_on_turn_still_reads_in_the_verdict`
  - `the_verdict_says_the_stock_was_turned_side_on`
  - `the_field_engine_refuses_the_side_on_carry_by_name`
- `crates/sim/tests/stock_carry_side.rs` (14 tests: exact block, steps on both sides, reversed axes, a filled cavity, a face inside a slab, a thin plate, there and back, the verdict, each refusal, the digest text)
- `crates/app/tests/setup_stock_source.rs`: `a_side_on_turn_between_setups_carries_and_a_skew_turn_is_refused_naming_the_turn` replaces the #866 test that pinned the side-on refusal. The test count of the file is the same.

Mutation checks. Each line was removed or changed, the named test went red, the file was restored, and `cmp` against the backup was identical:

| Line | Test that went red |
|---|---|
| non-finite refusal (`SideTurn::from_matrix`) | `turns_off_the_quarter_are_refused_by_name` |
| off-quarter entry refusal | same |
| not-a-permutation refusal | same |
| mirror refusal | same |
| not-side-on refusal | same |
| field-engine refusal | `the_field_engine_refuses_a_side_on_turn_by_name` |
| too-tall refusal | `a_body_too_tall_for_the_turned_lattice_is_refused_by_name` |
| high-side pad (never short) | `a_step_turned_side_on_is_never_read_short` |
| low-side pad (never short) | `a_step_on_the_low_side_is_never_read_short_either` |
| floor flag dropped after the turn | `a_clean_block_turned_side_on_reads_no_gouge_and_no_judged_floor` |
| slab counted whole | `a_face_inside_a_slab_counts_the_slab_whole` |
| gouge kept before a side-on turn | `a_gouge_cut_before_a_side_on_turn_still_reads_in_the_verdict` |
| side-on note on the gate | `the_verdict_says_the_stock_was_turned_side_on` |
| note only for a side-on carry | same |
| lattice-turn digest text | `the_two_kinds_of_turn_are_told_apart` |

Gate. `cargo xtask gate quick --dry-run` selected about 180 app suites, because the gate map of many suites names `sim::stock_sim`. The run was therefore done by name:

- sim: every suite of the quick plan (the lib and 32 test binaries), all green.
- app: the lib (313 tests) and `setup_carry_side`, `setup_stock_source`, `setup_carry`, `carried_verify`, `rest_across_setups`, `carried_engine_agreement`, `carried_fixtures_cache`, `carried_corner_rest`, `between_setups`, `setups`, `setup_align`, `stock_sim_document`, `post_not_judged`, `stock_engine_agreement`, `stock_view`, `fixtures`, `probe_only_sim`, all green.
- ui: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib setup_stock` (4 tests), green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`, clean.

## What was not exercised

- The batch tier and the other app suites of the quick plan.
- The pixel snapshots. No snapshot PNG changed.
- Windows and macOS. The run was on Linux.
- The prior plan on a job thread (`PriorPlan::simulate`) with a side-on turn. Its change is one call (`carry_through`).
- A carried fixture at a turned face. See the known limits.

## Known limits

- A wall that the tool flank cut, or a step, is read up to one cell outside the real face after the turn. The verdict can show rest of up to one cell on a finished face. The carried-fixture law (#321) can refuse a fixture that touches such a face. The workaround is the setup's own stock. The follow-up issue for the exact carry is linked in the issue comments.

- The verdict taken before the turn does not credit the edge breaks and marks of the earlier setup. The fold for a new block (#320) has the same limit.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/874-side-on-carry.md`. Branch from upstream `main` at 6c33940d.

Changelog: A setup turned side-on (a quarter turn about X or Y) can take the machined stock of the setup before it; the carried stock is never smaller than the real stock, and a gouge cut before the turn stays in the verdict.

title: fix(build): run independent release gate lanes in parallel
body:
## What changed

The release gate prebuilds debug and release test targets before running suites.
It runs up to four independent lanes together and mixes debug and release lanes.
It keeps app, kernel, UI and clippy steps alone.
App and kernel contain the import watchdogs.
Each lane keeps its own numbered log and wall time.
The summary reports total wall time and summed lane time as a serial estimate.
The gate stops after a failed prebuild and preserves checkout VOID checks.
The release lockfile guard accepts unchanged lines whose endings changed between LF and CRLF.
It still refuses changed package names and checksums.

## Cause

The gate ran every step serially.
The lockfile guard counted line-ending churn as nonversion changes.

## Tests

The prebuild and CRLF pins failed before the fixes.
Pins: `release_prebuilds_both_profiles_before_running_suites` and `lock_diff_guard_ignores_only_line_ending_changes`.
Additional pins cover four lanes, profile mixing, exactly-once scheduling, isolation and selected runs.

title: fix(post): refuse unsupported Sodick angle-word moves
body:
## What changed

Keep Sodick constant taper refused until its mapping preserves the generated wire path.
Refuse WireAngle records by operation name even when the section omits WireTaper.
Stop cutting that section instead of silently writing a vertical move.

The post ignored WireAngle records.
A direct angle-word stream without WireTaper could therefore emit a vertical cut without a warning.
Lower-guide XY and explicit upper-guide offsets cannot simply become nominal A angles without proving the corner and transition motion.
The alternative angle stream uses work-relative WirePlane, which does not establish Sodick's table-relative program height.

Sodick's [2012 LN1W/LN2W training manual](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/content/tools/sodick_edm/sodick_user_manual_small.pdf), printed pages 66-70, describes G51/G52, A, G50 and the table/guide settings.
That newer-control source does not prove the complete mapping for this post's Mark 21/EX21 target.
Unconfirmed items are Mark 21/EX21 TP/TN initialization and datum/calibration correspondence, corner and lead/cancel interpolation, and the signed angle mapping in that frame.
No unconfirmed words are emitted.

`sodick_refuses_angle_words_even_without_section_taper` fails on the original post and passes with the guard.
It covers positive, negative and zero angles.
`sodick_vertical_stream_still_posts_without_angle_words` preserves vertical posting.

title: fix(3d): a whole-model 3D Pocket clears an open-sided notch past its edge
body:
## What changed

A whole-model 3D Pocket used the model's silhouette as its footprint, and the level law erodes that by the tool radius. So the cutter's edge never passed the silhouette. On a notch open to the part's outside, the pocket left a band one radius wide along the open edges at the full stock height, and the op reported `ok` (#1749).

- `camcraft-motion`: new `machining3d::open_sides` (`machining3d/open_side.rs`). It grows the silhouette by the tool radius less 0.01 mm, minus a keep-out region. Where a level is open, the cutter centre now goes up to the silhouette edge. Where a level's material stands flush with the silhouette, the band is narrower than the erosion, so it cuts nothing there and a plain block gets no new ring.
- `camcraft-app`: the new `operation/open_side.rs` applies this footprint in the Pocket3D arm and in the Multi-Axis Rough arm (the stamped twin: one ladder). It applies only to the source-built footprint of an untilted whole-model source. A picked or Boundary-controlled region, and a tilted plane, stay as before. The keep-out is the silhouette of the setup's other parts.
- `keep_law::kept_models`: the setup's other parts now go into the solid law for Pocket3D and Multi-Axis Rough as a second net. This net also reports a cut through a second part that stands inside the model's own silhouette. Before, that cut read `ok` (the ladder's islands come only from its own model).
- `shared_face_bodies`: the #1706 pin (`the_sample_as_imported_refuses_the_3d_pocket_by_name`) pinned the old law. No 6 mm tool fit inside the 6.53 mm strip, so the op refused. Under the new law the pocket clears the stock beside the strip with no gouge. The pin is renamed to `the_sample_as_imported_roughs_the_3d_pocket_beside_its_silhouette`. Recorded in `docs/decisions/1749-pocket3d-open-side.md`.
  - The sample op does NOT post with the job's tool (takeover commit 82c9f082b). `EM-0600-4FL` has 15 mm of flute and an 8 mm shank; the part is 118 mm tall. Verify names `shank_hit` (part) and `rapid_in_stock` (the lifts out of those cuts), all `blocks_post`, and holds the post by R1. The test now deletes S1 (so the program gate runs) and asserts this reading by name: status `ok`, gate ran and passed, no gouge, only these two kinds, all on R1, `ok: false`, `held_by: [R1]`. Then it gives the tool 125 mm flutes and a 6 mm shank, generates again, and asserts a clean verify.
  - Cause: the 3D Pocket ladder keeps only the flute radius off the material above a level. The same R1 moves with full-depth flutes give no findings. A closed cavity with no open side gives the same kinds with main's footprint law and with this PR's law. So the shank blindness is on main; this PR only gives the sample a path. It is owed in #1844 (P3).

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_open_side.rs`. The fixture is built in code: a 30 mm block with its +X+Y quadrant notched down to Z 20, in a stock that fits it in XY with its top at Z 32. The tool is a 10 mm flat end mill, with offset rings and shell on.
- `an_open_sided_notch_is_cleared_to_the_parts_edge`: measures the stock the path leaves (the lowest flat-end disc over each column) along both open edges, 0.05 mm inside the part edge. It must be at the floor, Z 20. It also checks that no feed disc enters the part's material at its Z, and that verify is clean. Before the fix, the stock stayed at Z 32.000 at (14.95, 10.80).
- `an_open_side_never_reaches_into_a_neighbouring_part`: a second part 1 mm past the +X open edge. No feed disc comes within R of it, verify is clean, and the +Y open edge is still cleared.
- `a_part_standing_in_the_notch_is_named_by_the_solid_law`: a second part on the notch floor, inside the model's silhouette, is reported (warnings > 0), not read as `ok`.

Mutation checks. Each mutation was reverted afterwards and the file compared byte-for-byte with its backup:
- `open_footprint` returns the region unchanged: the open-edge test fails (stock at Z 32.000).
- Keep-out made empty: the neighbour test fails (81 solid-law warnings; the second net fires).
- The `keep_law` line removed: the neighbour test and the solid-law test both fail.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the Pocket3D-only version of the change: motion suites ok. App suites ok except `operations::multiaxis_rough_peels_the_same_ladder_and_poses_its_walls` (150 vs 134 moves). That failure led to the Multi-Axis Rough change. The #1706 pin also failed there; it is updated as described above.

- `generate.rs` stays at 3668 lines (this PR adds 11). Its split is owed and is not done here.

title: fix(post): Tormach lathe G76 J makes LinuxCNC's R1 ladder cut the record's passes
body:
## What changed

`assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps`, `g76Grid`: J (first depth) is no longer floored to the grid on its own. LinuxCNC's G76 with `R1` cuts J, 2J, ... with the last pass clamped at K, so the control cuts ceil(K/J) passes. The record lays n = ceil(height / first depth) equal rungs (g76Why already holds the equal ladder), so J must satisfy (n-1)J < K <= nJ:

- J is the shallower grid rounding (as before) when that keeps the count;
- when the shallower J would add a pass, J is the one grid step up, and never a full grid step over the record's first cut;
- otherwise the record is refused by name: `G76 threading cycle refused - no first depth J on the control's grid makes R1's equal ladder cut the record's n passes (K ...)`.

The root keeps its outward rounding. Peak, root, I and K are unchanged.

## Golden change, line by line

`crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/thread_g76_inch.nc`, one line:

```
-G76 P0.07874 Z0.315 I-0.004 J0.0314 K0.0944 R1 Q0 H0
+G76 P0.07874 Z0.315 I-0.004 J0.0315 K0.0944 R1 Q0 H0
```

What this relies on, from the public LinuxCNC G-code reference (G76): J is the first cut depth, K the full thread depth (diameters here, under G7), and `R1.0` selects constant depth, so each pass goes J deeper than the last and the last pass is clamped at K.
- Old: 0.0314, 0.0628, 0.0942, then 0.0944 (a 0.0002 in pass) = 4 passes. The record laid and the verdict judged 3 (0.4 / 0.8 / 1.2 mm radius).
- New: 0.0315, 0.0630, 0.0944 (clamped) = 3 passes, the record's count. J 0.0315 in is 0.000004 in (0.1 um) over the record's Ø0.8 mm first cut. The root (X + I - K) is the same as before: never deeper than the minor.
- P, Z, I, K, R, Q, H and every other line are unchanged. The mm golden (`J0.8 K2.4`) is byte-identical.

**Replaces #437** (opened from the old fork, which cannot take pushes). The parents #516 (#416) and #517 (#417) are merged on main. This PR now holds only the #418 work.

## What changed
- **The option:** `ThreadInfeed.repeat_each_depth`, off by default. Each pass above the root is followed by an identical copy: the same tip depth, the same lattice shift, the same helix phase. Thus a repeat cannot cut deeper and cannot move. The finishing pass and the spring passes at the root are not repeated.
- **Alternating infeed:** the side flips one time for each depth, not for each cut. Thus a repeat keeps its flank.
- **G76 refuses it by name, on the two lathe posts.** The record carries a `repeat_each_depth` flag. The stream writes it as `REP 1` only when it is set. The post property is `RepeatEachDepth`.

- **Defaults are byte-identical:** the stamp adds one byte only when the flag is on. No project key and no stream word is written when it is off. No version rung. No golden changed.

title: fix(post): G76 words state the thread passes that were verified
body:
**Replaces #433** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #432 (#416).** Part of #363.

## What changed
**With the G76 cycle post option, the G76 words now describe the passes the verdict judged.** G32 passes stay the default output.
- The record maps 1:1: `G76 P(m)(r)(a) Q(dmin) R(d)` / `G76 X Z P(k) Q(dd) F`, where:
  - dd = the first pass's depth;
  - dmin = the step (constant depth) or the plan's minimum (constant area);
  - d = the finishing pass's own depth;
  - m = 1 + spring passes;
  - a = twice the flank angle.
- **Control model** (GSK988TA, Fanuc-compatible G76):
  - each roughing pass goes to `max(dd·√n, previous + dmin)`, up to k − d;
  - the first finishing pass cuts d, and m − 1 more repeat at k;
  - each pass starts `depth·tan(a/2)` along Z.
- **Refused by name with G76 chosen:** alternating infeed (the CL carries a new `alternating` flag; `ALT 1` is written to the stream only when set), a doubled angle outside 0/29/30/55/60/80 (so 29.5° is refused), and a one-pass thread.

**⚠ This changes posted output for the default G76 thread: `R0` becomes `R0.4`.** The golden `fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc` changes on one line: `G76 P010000 Q400 R0` → `G76 P010000 Q400 R0.4`.
- Why: with `R0` the control roughs 0.4, 0.8 and 1.2, then cuts its finishing pass at the root again. That is a fourth full-depth pass the verdict never judged. It is not a gouge, but it is not what was verified.
- With `R0.4` it roughs 0.4 and 0.8 and finishes at 1.2: the three passes we judge.
- Making `R0` true instead would have meant changing G32 output and the judged passes.
- Note: the #363 research said Q = infeed made the control cut a decreasing ladder. That is not so, because dmin = infeed clamps every step equal. The real gap was R.

**R comes from the rounded words' own ladder (M3 review fix, head 0bb37ddd).** The control reads the posted words, each rounded to the least increment on its own. In inch, `Q157 P472 R0.0157` left k − d = 0.0315 one increment past the second rung 0.0314, so the control cut a 4th, unverified pass. Now the post counts the record's rough passes N from its own ladder, rebuilds rungs N−1 and N from the rounded Q (first depth), Q (minimum depth) and P (thread height), and writes the R whose last rough depth P − R lies in (rung N−1, rung N], nearest the record's allowance. Inch golden: `R0.0158` (control: 0.0157 / 0.0314 / 0.0472). If that R is more than one least increment from the record's allowance, the cycle is refused by name (the Q/Q/P words and the R window are named). The other G76 words (X, Z, P k, Q dd, Q dmin) are each one record value rounded once, not differences, so R was the only derived word. The Tormach (LinuxCNC) G76 has the same class of gap in J/K (inch `J0.0314 K0.0944` = ceil 4 passes for a 3-pass record), filed as #1619. Its goldens are left byte-identical to main here.

**A project cached before this PR posts R0 until the op is regenerated.** Checked: the stale stamp (`crates/app/src/operation/stamp.rs`, `current_stamp`) hashes only the operation's inputs (tool, params, source, heights). It has no generator version, and the cached record's `finish_allowance` reads back as saved (0). So such an op reads **Fresh**, not Stale:
- The Fanuc post writes `R0` for it: the output of main before this PR (one extra root pass in mm), not a gouge.
- The Tormach post refuses it by name, because it expects the ladder's last step. That is safe, but the message does not tell the user to regenerate the operation. Follow-up: #1843 (P7).

`docs/decisions/417-g76-matches-verified.md`

## How tested
- New app `lathe_post_g76_schedule` (4 tests):
  - a new flank, constant-area golden `thread_g76_area.nc` (`G76 P020055 Q100 R0.05` / `G76 X9.6 Z14 P1200 Q400 F2`): the control's schedule computed from the posted words matches the laid depths and stations within 1 µm (under the readings that the post uses; see "Not proven" below);
  - the default (`R0.4`) and a 0.5 step (`Q500 R0.2`) also match;
  - one refusal per unexpressible option;
  - `ALT` survives the stream and the project file.
- M3 review fix (head 0bb37ddd), two new tests in `lathe_post_g76_schedule`:
  - `the_default_thread_g76_states_its_three_passes_in_inch`: posts the default thread under G20, parses the G76 words, runs the control's ladder on them, and asserts exactly 3 passes matching the laid depths (`R0.0158`).
  - `a_ladder_the_rounded_words_cannot_state_is_refused_by_name`: two hand-edited inch records (13 and 39 sqrt rungs, 2 and 4 increments off) are refused by name, and the same record in mm posts.

## Not proven: four Fanuc G76 readings (no Fanuc control run exists)
No source that we read states these readings, and no run on a Fanuc control or simulator confirms them. In the list, k is the thread height and a the tool angle (twice the flank angle).
1. **Z-shift sign, and which pass sits at the programmed Z.** The post follows LinuxCNC's sign and sets the start Z to `c_first - k·tan(a/2)`. If the control shifts the other way, or its finishing pass sits at the programmed start Z, the whole thread moves axially by `k·tan(a/2)` to `2k·tan(a/2)` (0.6 to 1.25 mm for `thread_g76_area.nc`, 2 mm lead). That is a cut in the wrong place.
2. **End-Z shift.** If the control also shifts the end of each pass by `depth·tan(a/2)`, the root pass ends `k·tan(a/2)` past the programmed end Z. At a shoulder, that can cut into the shoulder.
3. **Minimum-depth clamp reading** (read as a per-pass minimum, per the manual's definition). A different reading changes the pass count or the per-pass depth only, never the root. It can give fewer, deeper passes than verified (the tool load is not judged). Equal-depth ladders (the default) are not affected.
4. **Rounding.** The pass count is fixed by construction (R from the rounded ladder, refused beyond one increment). Single rungs of a long sqrt ladder can still differ from the laid ones by a few increments. That is not a gouge.

Items 1 and 2 can move a flank thread (a ≠ 0) axially, or into a shoulder. They stay unproven without a Fanuc control run. The default radial thread (a = 0) has no Z shift, so items 1 and 2 do not change it. Main already carries the risk of items 1 and 2 for flank threads (#416 posts the angle and the start); this PR does not add it. Items 3 and 4 do not move the cut. The Fanuc run (or a refusal or warning for a flank G76 until the run) is tracked in #1842.

The PathPilot Hub simulation cannot check items 1-4: its lathe is LinuxCNC's one-block G76, not Fanuc's two-block G76. A Hub run is not needed for the Tormach side: the Tormach lathe goldens are byte-identical to main (checked against upstream/main). Only Fanuc-lathe goldens change (`thread_g76.nc` mm and inch, new `thread_g76_area.nc`). The inch Fanuc golden reads `R0.0158`.

Changelog: G76 threading output states the passes that were verified: the finish allowance R is posted (default threads now post R0.4 instead of R0), and options G76 cannot express are refused by name (#417)

Fixes #417

body:
The stack parents #517 (#417) and #518 (#418) are merged. The diff now holds only the #419 work.

## Merge-time refresh (maintainer's session, head 39632f647)
The maintainer's session took this PR over for a merge-time refresh. It merged `origin/main` (62e1d36a6) into the branch. It did not rebase or force-push.

Hand-resolved hunks (keep both sides):
- `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`, `threadHalfTurn`: the PR's dip chain is kept. Main changed the lead word from `fr()` to `fl()` (#902: an inch lead has six decimals). Both G32 blocks of the chain (the plain block and the dip block `G32 X Z F`) now use `fl()`. The three refusals of the chain (no open chain, steeper than 45 degrees, deeper than the pass) are kept.
- `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`, manifest: `continuousThreading = true` with its citation, and main's `workOffsetIndex`, `workOffsetMax`, `explainWords`, `explainTool`, `programUnits`, `explains`, `commentMax`, `explainBlockMax`.
- `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`, G76 header comment: the PR's chip-break dips clause and main's `g76Allowance` paragraph (#517). `g76Why` keeps the two refusals: `RepeatEachDepth` (#518) and `ChipBreakDips`.
- `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`: main's manifest list with `continuousThreading` added ("the last nine").
- `crates/post/src/post/engine.rs`: the `ChipBreakDips` refusal and main's `MillSpindle` reverse refusal (#988).
- `crates/post/src/post/js.rs`: the `continuous_threading` and `mill_spindle_reverse` fields.

No refusal of #517, #518 or main is lost. The Tormach lathe post does not declare `continuousThreading`, so the engine refuses dips on it by name. Its G76 `RepeatEachDepth` refusal (#518) is unchanged. `git diff origin/main --stat` lists only the 26 files of this PR.

Readings after the refresh (`cargo test -j 6 -p <crate> --test <binary>`, one binary at a time):
- camcraft-motion: `turning_thread_dips` 9/9, `turning_thread_cycle` 3/3, `turning_thread_infeed` 10/10, lib 366 passed (5 ignored).
- camcraft-post: `inverted_post` 16/16, `recorded_streams` 12/12, lib 54/54.
- camcraft-cl: lib 41/41.
- camcraft-app: `lathe_post_thread_dips` 6/6 (golden `thread_g32_dips.nc` unchanged), `lathe_post_g76` 8/8, `lathe_post_g76_schedule` 7/7, `lathe_post_tormach_thread` 8/8, `lathe_post_css` 10/10, `turning_thread` 10/10, `turning_thread_infeed` 5/5, `lathe_thread_travel` 2/2, `conformance` 7/7, `coarse_laws` 6/6, `lathe_field_tools` 2/2, `project_roundtrip` 73/73.
- camcraft-ui: lib filter `thread` 6/6.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Not exercised by the refresh: an inch program with dips (the `fl()` lead word under G20 has no golden), and a run on a controller or a simulator.

MCP: the dips ride the generic `edit_operation` tool through the project params JSON (`ThreadInfeedDto.dips`). No new MCP tool is necessary.

Screenshots: before and after screenshots on the refreshed head are in the section "Screenshots (Passes tab)" below.

Note: `crates/post/src/post/engine.rs` (600 lines) and `js.rs` (529 lines) were already more than 400 lines on main. This PR adds 4 and 17 lines to them.

## The citation gate (the issue's precondition)
Before any code, the issue required a primary-source citation that chained Fanuc G32 blocks keep spindle synchronization. Found in *FANUC Series 0i-TD/0i Mate-TD USER'S MANUAL (For Lathe System)*, B-64304EN-1/01, Part II:
- **§3.4 "Continuous Threading", p.34:** consecutive threading blocks keep "the synchronism with the spindle" at "the joint between blocks wherever possible", so the lead and shape can change midway.
- **§3.2 "Constant Lead Threading (G32)", WARNING 6, p.32:** a threading block that follows a threading block starts "without waiting for detection of the one-spindle-rotation signal".
- **§3.2, pp.29-31:** G32 cuts tapers (`G32 X41.0 Z29.0 F3.5`). Up to 45° the lead F is taken along Z.

The manual was read from a public third-party mirror of Fanuc's PDF (https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/fanuc-0itd-users-manualpdf/259106078), for behaviour only. The Haas G32 reference (cited in #363) agrees. **LinuxCNC G33 stays unconfirmed:** its docs don't say whether a chained G33 waits for the index again, so no LinuxCNC post may declare the capability.

## What changed
- **Parameters.** The infeed plan gains `ThreadInfeed.dips` with interval, height and length. An interval of 0 means off, which is the default.
- **Shape of a dip.** A dip is a radial lift on **roughing passes only**. Each ramp stays under 45°, keeping the lead on Z.
  - **Never placed in:** the first or last lead, or the finishing, spring or #418 repeat passes.
  - **Height:** no more than every dipped pass's depth of cut.
- **New CL segment.** A dip is a variable-radius XY half-turn: the axial travel is still exactly half a lead, but the end radius differs from the start.
- **Marking.** The thread record carries `chip_break_dips`: `DIP 1` in the stream, `ChipBreakDips` as a post property, and a project cache key only when set. The section carries `PARAM ChipBreakDips`. If dips are on but the record can't be attached, the kernel refuses, so a dip is never laid unmarked.
- **Post capability flag.** The engine refuses dips by name for any script without `continuousThreading = true`. Only `fanuc-lathe.cps` declares it, with the citation in its header.
  - It writes each dip segment as `G32 X Z F`.
  - It refuses by name a segment that doesn't continue a G32 chain, is steeper than 45°, or goes deeper than its plunge.
  - **G76 refuses dips by name.**
- **Verdict.** `thread_warnings` checks every chain for phase (equal axial advance per half-turn), depth, slope and placement. Any breach is a Gouge, which blocks the post.
- **UI.** Three rows on the Passes tab.
- **Defaults are byte-identical.** With dips off there is no stamp byte, project key, stream word or PARAM.
- `docs/decisions/419-thread-dips.md`

## How tested
- **New motion `turning_thread_dips`** (8 tests):
  - dips off lay the plain path bit for bit;
  - a dip is never deeper than its pass;
  - the phase is unchanged across the chain;
  - placement and slope rules hold;
  - a repeated depth cuts whole;
  - the verdict is silent on laid dips;
  - the verdict convicts each broken law (first/last lead, finishing pass, deeper, phase shift, steep). Temporarily disabling the laws made this test fail.
  - refusals by name.
- **New app `lathe_post_thread_dips`** (6 tests):
  - the golden `thread_g32_dips.nc`;
  - the posted chain keeps the plain thread's Z words and lead;
  - G76 refuses;
  - a post without `continuousThreading` refuses;
  - the lathe script refuses a bent dip;
  - dips ride the command, the stream and the project file.
- **Existing suites green:** the turning thread, infeed and G76 suites, `inverted_post`, `lathe_post*`, `project_roundtrip`, `conformance`, and all cl and post tests. No existing golden changed.
- `clippy -D warnings --all-targets` on motion, post, cl, app and ui is clean.

## Not exercised (draft)
- **Machine check:** a run on a lathe simulator or machine.
- **GUI check:** the Passes-tab rows. The #416 test kit covers the neighbouring rows.

Changelog: Threading: optional in-pass chip-break dips on roughing passes, posted as continuous G32 X Z F segments by the Fanuc lathe post (#419)

Fixes #419

The page header still reads "Contour1": the harness retypes the draft of the seeded operation, not the operation itself. Dip height and Dip length show only when Chip-break every is not 0.
